subject: 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrtul
fact: The date marks the second day of the party’s operation against the cult. It is when Pelek remains tied, the ritual resumes, and the Ember Vanguard launches their attack. It is the temporal anchor for the battle’s events.

subject: 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrtul
fact: The second day of the second tenday of Myrtul is when the group awakens to find Pelek still tied up. Grygum collects his winnings from JimJar’s bet. Pelek reflects on sleep and death. The group then departs from Buppido’s lair to re-infiltrate the cultist cavern, where they observe a distracted Derro and a new two-headed stone giant statue.

subject: Acid Vomiting Ritual

subject: attack on the cult
fact: The Ember Vanguard launches a coordinated assault using Zalthir’s darkness, Daz’s Scorching Rays, Grygum’s acid vomiting and guiding bolt, Thorin’s melee strikes, and Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp. The Ettin survives, Narrak is trapped, and the ritual is halted mid-incantation.

subject: curse spreading claim
fact: Narrak claims, 'You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!'
source_quote: You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Darkness Ambush
fact: Zalthir casts a magical darkness over the Derro and Ettin, obscuring vision and enabling surprise attacks; the environment becomes chaotic, with combatants striking blindly and magical effects interfering with perception.
source_quote: Zalthir and I had discussed what we should do. He plans to use his darkness...", "From inside it, Narrak shouts...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on where he thought Narrak was.
source_quote: I could keep them there with a spell. And so I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on where I think he is.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz cast scorching rays — three spears of flame — toward the Ettin, feeling invigorated and empowered.
source_quote: Three spears of flame, raging hues of orange and red, appear above me. My skin prickles and sweats under their intense heat—but I am not frightened. I feel invigorated. Empowered. These are the vessels of my inner fury.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz explained that there is no danger from Pelek/Derro and that tying him up would make them safer, referencing the past death of a group member at Buppido's hands.
source_quote: Daz, however, explains that there is no such danger. And that they would all be safer with the ghost tied up. The last time they trusted someone, Buppido killed one of their group.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the Derro avoided noticing them because they were trying to avoid being seen by Narrak, like how Priestesses of Lolth made others invisible out of fear.
source_quote: I finally understand why that Derro, who should have seen us, has not noticed us. He’s trying to avoid being seen by Narrak. I’ve seen that before, when the various Priestesses of Lolth would get angry, and everyone tried hard to be invisible.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz whispered to the Ember Vanguard that the Derro are performing a summoning ritual to make the Stone Giants sprout a second head, which probably explains what happened to the Stone Giant that fought them in the Dark Lake District.
source_quote: I turn and whisper to the Ember Vanguard, "They are performing some kind of summoning ritual to make the Stone Giants sprout a second head. This probably explains what happened to the Stone Giant that fought us in the Dark Lake District."

subject: Daz’s recognition of Lolth’s Priestesses

source_quote: I’ve seen that before, when the various Priestesses of Lolth would get angry, and everyone tried hard to be invisible. A high-level cleric can kill you very easily.

subject: Ritual of Demogorgon

The ritual’s effects are believed to have altered a Stone Giant in the Dark Lake District. The group observes the ritual but delays intervention, trusting Hgraam to reverse its effects.

subject: Zalthir’s darkness manipulation
fact: Zalthir manipulates his darkness spell to counter Narrak’s fear spell by obscuring the caster’s visibility.
source_quote: I move the darkness over Narrak. As the source of the Ember Vanguard’s fear is no longer visible, they are no longer affected by it.

subject: Zalthir’s darkness used tactically
fact: Zalthir uses darkness not only for concealment but as a tactical tool to disrupt Narrak’s fear spell by moving it over the caster.
source_quote: I move the darkness over Narrak. As the source of the Ember Vanguard’s fear is no longer visible, they are no longer affected by it.

subject: Zalthir’s final realization
fact: Zalthir realizes the statue is only two feet tall after being shown it, correcting his initial assumption of its size.
source_quote: I look at him confused, and I show him the statue on the platform. He sighs as he realizes it is only 2 feet tall.

subject: Zalthir’s fire breath
fact: Zalthir breathes fire into his darkness, but is disappointed with the outcome.
source_quote: Zalthir rushes into his darkness and breathes fire. He seems disappointed with the outcome.

subject: Zalthir’s fire breath disappointment
fact: Zalthir is disappointed with the outcome of his fire breath in the darkness, suggesting it was ineffective against the Derro.
source_quote: Zalthir rushes into his darkness and breathes fire. He seems disappointed with the outcome.

subject: Zalthir’s fire breath in darkness
fact: Zalthir breathes fire into his magical darkness, targeting the concealed Derro, but is disappointed with the outcome.
source_quote: Zalthir rushes into his darkness and breathes fire. He seems disappointed with the outcome.

subject: Zalthir’s meditation interrupted
fact: Zalthir attempts to meditate but is interrupted by the Myconid, who insists on talking about Rump-a-dump and the nature of myconid-zombie conversion.
source_quote: I look forward to meditating when my thoughts are interrupted. ... “Zalthir, you never listen to anything I say. It’s not fair. Why don’t you listen to me!”

subject: Zalthir’s meditation interrupted by Myconid
fact: Zalthir’s attempt at meditation is persistently interrupted by the Myconid’s emotional demands about Rump-a-dump and non-violence.
source_quote: I look forward to meditating when my thoughts are interrupted. ... “Zalthir, you never listen to anything I say. It’s not fair. Why don’t you listen to me!”

subject: Zalthir’s monk training
fact: Zalthir’s monk training allows him to resist the madness induced by the ritual circle.
source_quote: There’s some kind of effect that the circle has on those who enter it. Some kind of madness gripped my mind, but my monk training allowed me to stop it. Be careful!

subject: Zalthir’s monk training against madness
fact: Zalthir’s monk training allows him to resist the madness induced by the ritual circle’s effect.
source_quote: There’s some kind of effect that the circle has on those who enter it. Some kind of madness gripped my mind, but my monk training allowed me to stop it. Be careful!

subject: Zalthir’s realization of statue size
fact: Zalthir initially believes the statue of the stone giant is massive, but is corrected when shown it is only two feet tall.
source_quote: I look at him confused, and I show him the statue on the platform. He sighs as he realizes it is only 2 feet tall.

subject: Zalthir’s statue realization
fact: Zalthir realizes the statue is only two feet tall after being shown it.
source_quote: I look at him confused, and I show him the statue on the platform. He sighs as he realizes it is only 2 feet tall.

subject: zombie conversion process
fact: The Myconids have a process that allows them to convert their dead enemies into zombies.
source_quote: we have this process that allows us to convert our dead enemies into zombies.

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: The Cult of Demogorgon, led by Narrak, performs rituals to graft second heads onto Stone Giants using Derro acolytes. Their goal is to empower Demogorgon by creating monstrous avatars to destroy Gracklstugh. They rely on chanted incantations, fear magic, and ritual precision, and are deeply hierarchical with Narrak as an authoritarian choir director.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a subterranean cult faction devoted to Demogorgon, performing ritualistic transformations and chants to empower their city’s doom; they are obedient to Narrak but lack discipline, requiring constant correction.
source_quote: He motions to all of the Derro to surround him...", "The Derro groan and gather around him.", "The Derro only do so half heartedly...

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a cohesive adventuring group focused on infiltrating and destroying the Demogorgon-worshipping cult. They use stealth, magic, and coordinated attacks. Members include Daz, Zalthir, Grygum, Thorin, and JimJar. They are distrustful of past betrayals and rely on divine intervention (Hgraam) and tactical patience.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a group of warriors bound by magical fear and ritual alignment with Narrak’s cult; they are susceptible to psychological manipulation and serve as both targets and unwitting enforcers of the ritual’s power.
source_quote: the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.", "They are bunched up; it’s time to attack.

subject: Myconid Circle
fact: A group of sentient fungi led by the Myconid who communicate via spores. They convert dead enemies into zombie-like entities and view themselves as nonviolent. They are emotionally invested in Rump-a-dump and seek reconciliation, but are misunderstood and feared by the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Buppido’s Lair
fact: Buppido’s Lair is a grim, bone-strewn site where the Ember Vanguard has previously faced betrayal. It serves as their base of operations and is referenced as the origin of past trauma, particularly the death of a party member by Buppido.

subject: Buppido’s lair
fact: Buppido’s lair is the group’s former base, now abandoned and grim, filled with dead bones and an altar to a demonic power. It is referenced as the site of a past betrayal where Buppido killed one of their group. The group departs from here to return to the cultist cavern.

subject: Buppido’s lair
fact: Buppido’s lair is the previous stronghold of the cult, from which the Ember Vanguard departs before returning to the cultist cavern.
source_quote: And so we head out from Buppido’s lair and find ourselves once again outside of the cultist cavern.

subject: Cultist Cavern
fact: The Cultist Cavern is a hidden chamber beneath Buppido’s lair where the Demogorgon cult performs its rituals. It contains a platform with a stone giant statue, a group of chanting Derro, an Ettin guard, and a head cultist named Narrak. The cavern is poorly lit and filled with the stench of brimstone.

subject: Cultist Cavern
fact: The cultist cavern is the site of repeated ritual activity targeting Demogorgon and the grafting of heads onto Stone Giants. It contains a central platform with a two-headed stone giant statue, five chanting Derro, an Ettin, a death dog, and a chief cultist holding the ritual book. The party has infiltrated it stealthily multiple times, with Derro often distracted or preoccupied. It is the focal point of the current mission to end the cult.

subject: cultist cavern
fact: The cultist cavern is the site of the ritual, where Derro chant around a platform with a two-headed stone giant statue, and where the Ember Vanguard sneaks in undetected.
source_quote: And so we head out from Buppido’s lair and find ourselves once again outside of the cultist cavern. And once again, we have managed to sneak into the room.

subject: cultist cavern location
fact: The cultist cavern is located outside of Buppido’s lair.
source_quote: outside of the cultist cavern

subject: darkness effect zone
fact: Zalthir’s magical darkness envelops the Derro and obscures Narrak’s vision.
source_quote: all the derro are covered in his magical darkness

subject: derro distraction target
fact: A Derro is preoccupied with a death dog, desperately trying hard not to be noticed.
source_quote: preoccupied with a death dog, desperately trying hard not to be noticed

subject: final resting place
fact: The final resting place is Buppido’s lair, a grim place full of dead bones and an altar to some demonic power.
source_quote: We are once again at the final resting place of Buppido. It’s a grim place, full of dead bones, and an altar to some demonic power or some mad idea.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the cult city targeted for destruction by the ritual; it is the ultimate goal of the two-headed transformation and the locus of the cult’s apocalyptic ambitions.
source_quote: they will lay waste to Gracklstugh!

subject: Monastery
fact: The monastery is referenced by Zalthir as a place where children were taught silence. He uses it as a metaphor to express his frustration with the Myconid’s incessant chatter and his desire for peace.

subject: platform
fact: The platform holds a statue of a stone giant with a second head emerging from it, and is surrounded by Derro during the ritual.
source_quote: There is a statue of another two-headed stone giant. ... They all move to their positions. ... A statue of a stone giant with a second head emerging from it.

subject: stone giant statue height
fact: The statue of a stone giant with a second head emerging from it is only 2 feet tall.
source_quote: it is only 2 feet tall

subject: Whorlstone's Depths
fact: Whorlstone's Depths is the mythic source of Demogorgon’s power, where spiraling rituals originate and madness flows upward into the cult’s city; it is referenced in chant as the origin of corruption.
source_quote: From Whorlstone's depths, the spirals turn!

subject: death dog
fact: A death dog is present in the cultist cavern, and one Derro is preoccupied with trying not to be noticed by it.
source_quote: There is a derro who, by all rights, should see us, but he seems to be preoccupied with a death dog, desperately trying hard not to be noticed.

subject: Death Dog
fact: A death dog is present in the cultist cavern, distracting a Derro who is desperately trying not to be noticed. The party successfully sneaks past because the Derro is occupied with the creature, allowing them to enter undetected.

subject: Demogorgon’s Influence
fact: Demogorgon’s presence manifests as madness, spiraling rituals, and physical corruption; its influence warps perception, causes acid vomiting, and empowers the cult’s rituals with terrifying, reality-bending effects.
source_quote: His madness flows, our city drools!", "Demogorgon’s madness flows through me!", "the curse spreads!

subject: Derro
fact: Derro are the chanting cultists who perform the ritual, are concealed by Zalthir’s darkness, attack Grygum and Zalthir, and are berated by Narrak for lack of vigor.
source_quote: Five Derro are chanting. ... One of the Derro raises a hand, and asks where, and the head cultist shouts, “OVER THERE!!!” ... Another Derro rushes out of Zalthir’s darkness and attacks Grygum, missing.

subject: derro count
fact: Five Derro are chanting.
source_quote: five Derro are chanting

subject: Ettin
fact: An Ettin is present near the cult’s central platform, positioned next to the obvious boss. It is observed by Daz and mentioned as part of the ritual’s defensive or symbolic arrangement. It is not directly engaged but is noted as a significant threat in the chamber.

subject: Ettin
fact: The Ettin is a two-headed creature targeted by Daz, struck by Thorin and Grygum, and attacks the frightened Thorin with its morning star.
source_quote: I say the Ettin. ... The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin, and misses, but the morning star hits. ... A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: ettin count
fact: An Ettin is present next to the obvious boss.
source_quote: an Ettin .

subject: Stone Giant (two-headed statue)
fact: A statue of a two-headed stone giant, two feet tall, stands at the center of the ritual platform. It is the focal point of the cult’s summoning ritual, which seeks to graft additional heads onto Stone Giants. Daz and Grygum link it to a prior encounter with a Stone Giant in the Dark Lake District. It is not alive but represents the ritual’s intended effect.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a cleric of the Ember Vanguard who understands cult tactics from Lolth's priesthood and targets the Ettin during the ritual assault. He casts Scorching Rays and Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp, and recognizes the Derro's fear of Narrak as analogous to Lolth's priestess dynamics.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is leading the group through another ritual targeting a demon, having witnessed the successful use of the ritual by the Drow. He observes the acrid stench of brimstone, eerie campfire atmosphere, and five Derro chanting in harmony. He identifies the central statue as a two-headed stone giant and correctly links it to a prior encounter with a Stone Giant in the Dark Lake District. He cautions Thorin against rushing in and notes the ritual’s source: a book in the chief cultist’s hands. He later hears the chant invoking Demogorgon and recognizes the ritual’s intent: grafting additional heads. He is aware that Grygum’s spells are nearly ready and that Hgraam may reverse the effects on Stone Giants. He is amused when Zalthir misunderstands the size of the statue, realizing it is only two feet tall.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who targets the Ettin during the ambush, and recognizes the behavior of Derro avoiding Narrak as similar to Priestesses of Lolth silencing their subordinates.
source_quote: I finally understand why that Derro, who should have seen us, has not noticed us. He’s trying to avoid being seen by Narrak. I’ve seen that before, when the various Priestesses of Lolth would get angry, and everyone tried hard to be invisible.

subject: Demogorgon
fact: Demogorgon is the demon invoked in the ritual chant, described as the Prince of Chaos whose madness flows through the cultists.
source_quote: For Demogorgon, the city will burn! ... Demogorgon’s madness flows through me!

subject: Derro
fact: A Derro is present in the cultist cavern, preoccupied with a death dog and failing to notice the party’s infiltration. He is possessed by Pelek, a ghost who fears losing control of him. The Derro’s body is used as a vessel, and his actions are under the influence of Pelek’s consciousness. He is restrained with knots that hold, as confirmed the next day.

subject: Derro
fact: A group of Derro chant the ritual incantation for Demogorgon, fail to perform with vigor, and are controlled by Narrak. They are blinded by Zalthir’s darkness, attack Grygum and Zalthir, miss their strikes, and are overwhelmed by the Ember Vanguard’s assault. One Derro is preoccupied avoiding Narrak’s notice.

subject: Ettin
fact: The Ettin is a two-headed monstrosity guarding the ritual platform, targeted by Daz during the attack. It wields a battle axe and morning star, is struck by Grygum’s guiding bolt and Thorin’s attack, and survives the initial assault with a smile after being damaged.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the city targeted by the cult’s ritual, which they intend to lay waste to after converting more Stone Giants.
source_quote: Now we shall convert one more, and by golly, they will lay waste to Gracklstugh!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of the Ember Vanguard who prepares spells to counter the cult’s effects, ties up Pelek/Derro, and later vomits acid in a violent reaction to ritual magic. He casts a guiding bolt at the Ettin, is affected by Narrak’s fear spell, and is the target of multiple Derro attacks. He collects a bet win from JimJar over knot durability.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric or divine caster who channels acid through violent ritual vomiting after being attacked; he survives lethal trauma and responds with potent, unorthodox magic, suggesting deep ties to chaotic or necrotic forces.
source_quote: Grygum moaning in pain, then in incantation. There is a violent heaving. I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is struck by a Derro, vomits acid after incantation, casts a guiding bolt at the Ettin, and is affected by Narrak’s fear spell before being freed by Zalthir’s darkness.
source_quote: One of the Derro rushes out of Zalthir’s darkness, notices Grygum, and strikes him while chanting, “You shall die! You shall die!” ... I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid. A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the one who notices the need to stop the ritual, but his spells are almost finished, and he later receives divine insight that Hgraam can reverse the ill effects on the Stone Giants.
source_quote: Grygum turns to me, “I know we want to stop this ritual, but my spells are almost finished.” ... We are told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is uncertain about the safety of Pelek/Derro and questions whether the ghost is a threat.
source_quote: At first, I am confused and uncertain. More to the point, are we safe with this ghost?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum prepares to pray when Pelek, now possessing a Derro body, asks to be tied up out of fear he might lose control and the Derro might kill them. Grygum is uncertain of their safety with the ghost. Daz reassures him, citing past betrayal by Buppido that resulted in a group member’s death. As they tie Pelek up, JimJar makes a bet that the knots won’t hold. The next day, Pelek remains tied, and Grygum collects his winnings. Upon untying him, Pelek reflects on the ambiguity of death and sleep, sparking a philosophical impulse in Grygum that is cut short by the need to prepare for battle. Grygum later reassures Thorin that Hgraam can handle the new two-headed stone giant statue, and their mission remains to end the cult.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is a divine agent of the Ember Vanguard believed capable of reversing the ill effects of the cult’s ritual on Stone Giants. Grygum and the party rely on Hgraam’s potential to undo the grafting magic, though Hgraam does not appear directly.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is a member of the group with the ability to reverse the ill effects inflicted upon Stone Giants by the cult’s ritual. Daz and Grygum both recognize this ability, and it is cited as the reason they can delay immediate action against the statue. It is implied Hgraam’s magic will mitigate the ritual’s grafting of additional heads.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is referenced as a divine entity who can reverse the ill effects on the Stone Giants, invoked by Grygum’s divine insight.
source_quote: We are told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants.

subject: JimJar
fact: JimJar bets Grygum that his knots on Pelek will not hold, and later loses the bet when Pelek remains tied up the next day.
source_quote: JimJar again offers one of his silly bets. He bets me that my knots won’t hold. ... And when we wake up, Pelek/Derro is still tied up. And I collect my winnings.

subject: JimJar
fact: JimJar is a member of the Ember Vanguard who places bets on mundane outcomes, including whether Grygum’s knots will hold. He is the source of comic relief and distraction during tense moments.

subject: JimJar
fact: JimJar is a recurring member of the group who makes frivolous bets. He bets Grygum that the knots restraining Pelek/Derro will not hold. His behavior is described as silly, and he is present during the tying of Pelek. Grygum wins the bet the next day.

subject: Myconid
fact: A Myconid communicates telepathically with Zalthir about Rump-a-dump, a dissatisfied member of her circle. She insists on nonviolence, equates her kind with zombies, and claims the group can convert enemies into undead. Zalthir grows frustrated with her persistence and eventually silences her by invoking parental advice.

subject: Myconid
fact: The Myconid is a persistent, emotionally driven creature who communicates through spores. She insists on resolving the matter of Rump-a-dump, a dissatisfied member of her circle whom she believes is being mistreated. She claims no one should be killed because the targets are like her, and reveals her kind’s ability to convert dead enemies into zombies. She becomes upset when Zalthir expresses fear of becoming one, accusing him of not helping her friends. She eventually falls asleep after Zalthir invokes parental wisdom, leaving him to reflect on her behavior.

subject: Myconid
fact: The Myconid speaks to Zalthir about Rump-a-dump, insists on non-violence toward her kind, and claims they convert enemies into zombies, before falling asleep after Zalthir’s frustration.
source_quote: The childlike voice of the Myconid. ... “Rump-a-dump would never let them do that! You don’t want to help my friends, and so why should I help you?” ... And the creature falls asleep.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the choir-like head cultist who directs the Derro’s ritual, uses fear magic, and is ultimately trapped by Daz’s spell.
source_quote: Silence, you blithering half-wits! More vigor! This city's doom, a ritual! Dig it! ... I will use fear! ... You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the head cultist leading a ritual to transform giants into two-headed monsters, demanding fervor and precision in chant and movement; he is the emotional and magical core of the Derro cult, and his madness drives their actions.
source_quote: Hear me, you two-headed fools! His madness flows, our city drools! From Whorlstone's depths, the spirals turn! For Demogorgon, the city will burn! More heads for grafting! More for the pile!

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the head cultist leading the ritual to graft second heads onto Stone Giants for Demogorgon. He is obsessed with ritual precision, shouts motivational commands, and is the source of a fear spell that affects the Ember Vanguard. He emerges from Zalthir’s darkness and screams about the inevitable spread of the curse after being trapped by Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the head cultist who leads the ritual chant, berates the Derro for lack of vigor, casts fear using a white feather, and is trapped in Zalthir’s darkness after being targeted by Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp.
source_quote: Silence, you blithering half-wits! More vigor! This city's doom, a ritual! Dig it! ... I will use fear! He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, says the magic words, and the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified. ... You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is a Derro possessed by a ghost who is tied up after concern he might lose control, and later speaks about death as a form of sleep while being untied.
source_quote: I haven’t had a good night's sleep in ages. Although it’s unclear if I am sleeping … There is this whole question about whether death is a form of sleep. I suppose I will find out.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is a ghost possessing the body of a Derro. He fears losing control of the Derro host and requests to be restrained. He acknowledges uncertainty about whether he is truly sleeping or dead. After being tied up, he expresses relief at having had a restful night — unusual for him — and muses on the philosophical question of whether death is a form of sleep.

subject: Pelek/Derro
fact: Pelek is a ghost possessing the body of a Derro, feared for losing control and potentially killing the party. He is tied up by the group after Daz reassures them that restraint is safer than trust, referencing past betrayal by Buppido. He mutters on the nature of death as sleep upon being untied.

subject: The Ettin
fact: The Ettin is a two-headed monstrosity serving as a frontline combatant for the Derro cult; it is resistant to magical damage, capable of wielding dual weapons, and is the primary target of the party’s assault.
source_quote: The Ettin points at the three of us outside of the darkness...", "The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin...", "A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a member of the Ember Vanguard rendered terrified by Narrak’s fear spell; he is struck by the Ettin’s morning star while incapacitated, indicating vulnerability to psychological magic.
source_quote: the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.", "The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin, and misses, but the morning star hits. Thorin looks battered.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a warrior of the Ember Vanguard who is cautious about rushing into battle, listens to Zalthir’s warnings, and is targeted by Narrak’s fear spell. He is struck by the Ettin’s morning star, survives the encounter, and expresses concern for the Stone Giants’ fate.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is eager to rush into the cultist chamber upon seeing the two-headed stone giant statue and later the Ettin. He is repeatedly cautioned by Daz and Zalthir, and he listens. He expresses concern for the safety of the giants, believing they need protection. He is displeased when told the effects on the Stone Giants might be reversed, but ultimately understands the need for patience. He points out the statue to Grygum, who reassures him Hgraam can handle it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is targeted by Narrak’s fear spell, is struck by the Ettin’s morning star while frightened, and attempts to strike the Ettin with success after the fear is broken.
source_quote: The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin, and misses, but the morning star hits. Thorin looks battered. ... But Thorin has a better chance to strike the creature, and he does.

subject: Whorlstone
fact: Whorlstone is the location from whose depths the spirals turn, referenced in the ritual chant as the origin of the magic.
source_quote: From Whorlstone's depths, the spirals turn!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir casts darkness to conceal the Derro, breathes fire into it, warns of a madness-inducing effect from the ritual circle, and later moves the darkness over Narrak to break the fear spell.
source_quote: There’s some kind of effect that the circle has on those who enter it. Some kind of madness gripped my mind, but my monk training allowed me to stop it. Be careful! I move the darkness over Narrak. As the source of the Ember Vanguard’s fear is no longer visible, they are no longer affected by it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a member of the Ember Vanguard who uses darkness magic to obscure the battlefield, coordinates attacks with the party, and employs tactical repositioning to counter magical effects; he is observant and decisive in combat.
source_quote: I want to watch!", "Let’s attack now.", "They are bunched up; it’s time to attack.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a monk of the Ember Vanguard who uses magical darkness to conceal the party during the ritual attack. He breathes fire, detects madness effects within the ritual circle, and misjudges the size of the stone giant statue as 2 feet tall. He is impatient with the Myconid’s persistent chatter and struggles to distinguish friend from foe among the undead myconids.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is impatient with the Myconid's persistent demands and has worn thin on his patience.
source_quote: My patience has worn thin. And at this time, in the monastery, the young children would have learned to be silent, I wonder if this creature can learn to be quiet.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is meditating when interrupted by a Myconid who insists on talking to Rump-a-dump, a dissatisfied member of her circle. The Myconid claims Rump-a-dump is connected to a prior group of ape-like creatures and insists no one should be killed because they are like her. Zalthir feigns ignorance, attempts to postpone the matter, and grows frustrated as the Myconid persists, claiming he never listens. The Myconid reveals their ability to convert dead enemies into zombies, alarming Zalthir. He warns he does not wish to become one. The Myconid becomes emotional, accusing him of not helping her friends. Zalthir, seeking quiet, invokes parental wisdom to calm the situation, and the Myconid falls asleep. He reflects on parental complaints while observing her slumber.

subject: acid vomit
fact: A violent, non-magical reaction experienced by Grygum after exposure to ritual magic. He vomits a wave of acid, which is not a spell he chose to cast but a consequence of the cult’s influence.

subject: Book in chief cultist’s hands
fact: A book held by the chief cultist is the source of the ritual chant used to summon Demogorgon and graft additional heads onto Stone Giants. Daz identifies it as the origin of the incantation, and Grygum later confirms its role in the cult’s magic.

subject: book in chief cultist's hands
fact: The book in the chief cultist's hands contains the ritual chant used by the Derro, and is referenced as the source of the incantation.
source_quote: Ah, the book in the chief cultist's hands.

subject: Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp
fact: A spell cast by Daz to trap Narrak in earthy tendrils. It successfully immobilizes the cult leader mid-ritual, causing him to scream about the inevitable spread of the curse.

subject: Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp
fact: Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp is cast by Daz to trap Narrak in the darkness, causing him to scream in rage.
source_quote: And so I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on where I think he is. ... Narrak screams in rage - “You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!”

subject: scorching rays
fact: A spell cast by Daz that summons three spears of flame to attack the Ettin. The spell is described as roaring like beasts and is fueled by Daz’s inner fury.

subject: scorching rays
fact: Daz casts three spears of flame as scorching rays, roaring with orange and red hues, aimed at the Ettin.
source_quote: Three spears of flame, raging hues of orange and red, appear above me. My skin prickles and sweats under their intense heat—but I am not frightened. I feel invigorated. Empowered. These are the vessels of my inner fury. They roar like fierce beasts as I hurl them toward the Ettin.

subject: statue of stone giant
fact: The statue is a two-headed stone giant, two feet tall, located on the platform, and is mistaken by Zalthir as being massive until he realizes its true size.
source_quote: I look at him confused, and I show him the statue on the platform. He sighs as he realizes it is only 2 feet tall.

subject: stone giant statue
fact: A two-headed stone statue of a Stone Giant, 2 feet tall, serves as the ritual focus for the cult’s grafting magic. Zalthir initially believes it to be massive, but realizes its true size, causing him to sigh in disbelief.

subject: white feather
fact: A white feather used by Narrak to cast a fear spell on the Ember Vanguard. It is the focus of the spell that induces terror in Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir until Narrak is obscured by darkness.

subject: White Feather
fact: The white feather is a ritual focus used by Narrak to cast fear magic; it is a symbolic tool of control, linking the caster’s will to the emotional state of the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir...

subject: white feather
fact: The white feather is used by Narrak to cast a fear spell on Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir.
source_quote: He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, says the magic words, and the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.

subject: Hgraam
fact: It is told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants, but the nature or source of this ability is not explained.
source_quote: We are told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants.

subject: Hgraam’s reversal capability
fact: The party’s belief that Hgraam can reverse the grafting magic on Stone Giants is an unconfirmed thread. No one has seen Hgraam, and the ritual’s damage remains unaddressed, leaving the fate of the giants uncertain.

subject: Invisibility to Derro
fact: The Derro fail to notice the party because they are actively avoiding detection by Narrak; this reveals a hierarchy of fear within the cult, where subordinates prioritize appeasing their leader over battlefield awareness.
source_quote: I finally understand why that Derro, who should have seen us, has not noticed us. He’s trying to avoid being seen by Narrak.

subject: nature of death and sleep
fact: A philosophical thread introduced by Pelek/Derro, who questions whether death is a form of sleep. The party does not resolve it, but it lingers as an existential undercurrent, especially as Pelek is bound and half-dead.

subject: Nature of death and sleep
fact: Pelek muses on whether death is a form of sleep, sparking philosophical interest in Grygum. The thread remains open, as no definitive answer is provided, and the group must continue their mission. The question lingers as a thematic undercurrent, especially given Pelek’s ghostly nature and the Myconid’s zombie conversion process.

subject: Pelek’s identity and control
fact: Pelek is a ghost possessing a Derro body and fears losing control of the host. The group ties him up as a precaution after a past betrayal led to a member’s death. Pelek questions whether death is a form of sleep, and his true intentions remain ambiguous. The thread remains open: is Pelek a trustworthy ally, a hidden threat, or something beyond comprehension?

subject: Rump-a-dump
fact: The Myconid insists Rump-a-dump is an unhappy sprout from their circle who needs to be brought back, but the reason for their unhappiness and connection to the ape-like creatures remains unresolved.
source_quote: Rump-a-dump is a sprout from my circle who is unhappy. We need to go talk to Rump-a-dump, find out what’s going on, and bring them back.

subject: Rump-a-dump’s fate
fact: The Myconid insists that Rump-a-dump, a member of her circle, is unhappy and needs to be retrieved. She claims Rump-a-dump is connected to a prior group of ape-like creatures and that no one should be killed because the targets are like her. Zalthir postpones the matter, but the Myconid remains emotionally fixated. The thread remains unresolved, with Zalthir uncertain whether the Myconids are friends or foes, and whether Rump-a-dump is a victim, a traitor, or something else.

subject: Rump-a-dump’s fate
fact: The Myconid’s unresolved plea about Rump-a-dump creates a narrative thread about nonviolence, conversion of enemies, and whether the myconids are allies or threats. Zalthir dismisses it, but the question remains open.

subject: the curse spreading
fact: Narrak’s final scream — 'The curse spreads!' — introduces a looming threat beyond the immediate battle. The nature of the curse is undefined, but its inevitability is emphasized, leaving the party to wonder what comes next.

subject: The Curse Spreads
fact: A lingering, inevitable curse tied to Demogorgon is spreading through the ritual; despite attempts to disrupt it, the curse persists, suggesting the cult’s doom is not just planned but predestined.
source_quote: Narrak screams in rage - 'You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!'
